neuroscience: Emerging evidence suggests that neuroinflammation contributes to age-related cognitive decline, yet the temporal progression of microglial activation remains unclear; here, longitudinal two-photon imaging revealed that microglial processes became progressively less motile in aging mice, coinciding with increased expression of pro-inflammatory transcripts. Spatial transcriptomics showed localized hotspots of NF-κB activation near synaptic-dense regions, and pharmacological inhibition of this signaling partially restored microglial surveillance dynamics. Our work defines a microglial timeline linking reduced surveillance to inflammation-associated synaptic loss.

Recent advances in circuit-level analysis have highlighted the need to understand how distributed neural ensembles coordinate perception and action; here, we investigated how prefrontal–striatal subnetworks encode context-dependent decisions using multiphoton imaging and optogenetic perturbations in mice. By combining latent-state modeling with cell-resolved activity maps, we found that ensembles dynamically reconfigure during rule switches, with inhibitory interneurons gating transitions between stable attractor states. Perturbation of parvalbumin-positive interneurons disrupted state transitions and produced characteristic behavioral inflexibility. Our findings demonstrate that flexible cognition depends on dynamic inhibitory sculpting of mesoscale ensemble activity.

The mechanisms by which astrocytes regulate synaptic efficacy during learning are poorly understood; we combined chemogenetic manipulation with fiber photometry to track astrocytic Ca²⁺ signaling in the motor cortex during a skilled reaching task. Learning induced heightened Ca²⁺ event synchrony that preceded synaptic potentiation measured by in vivo electrophysiology. Inhibiting Gq-coupled astrocytic signaling impaired performance gains and reduced dendritic spine stabilization. Thus, astrocytic Ca²⁺ coordination appears essential for reinforcing experience-dependent synaptic plasticity.

Neural computations underlying visual motion integration remain incompletely characterized; using a naturalistic motion cloud stimulus, we recorded from populations of neurons in primate MT while applying closed-loop microstimulation. Hierarchical Bayesian modeling showed that neurons jointly encode velocity gradients and local texture cues, and microstimulation shifted perceptual decisions toward the encoded subspace. Our findings support a predictive coding account of motion integration.

Understanding reward prediction errors in distributed cortical–subcortical networks requires cell-type-specific recording; to address this, we performed simultaneous calcium imaging of dopaminergic terminals and striatal spiny neurons during reinforcement learning in mice. Dopaminergic transients encoded bidirectional prediction errors, while spiny neurons exhibited ensemble-specific tuning corresponding to value updates. Optogenetic disruption of temporally precise dopaminergic bursts selectively impaired positive but not negative reinforcement. These results highlight complementary coding schemes for reward computation.

Although hippocampal oscillations are known to organize memory-relevant activity, their role in rapid integration of spatial and contextual cues remains unclear; we examined theta–gamma coupling during a virtual navigation task in humans implanted with depth electrodes. Using cross-frequency decomposition, we observed task-dependent increases in slow-gamma nesting within theta troughs when participants encountered novel spatial boundaries. Encoding strength correlated with gamma-burst precision, and computational modeling suggested enhanced phase-to-amplitude transfer efficiency. These results support a mechanism wherein theta-dependent gamma modulation facilitates rapid contextual binding.

The neural basis of multisensory integration remains incompletely understood; we used high-density laminar probes in mouse superior colliculus to quantify how auditory and visual cues combine to guide orienting behavior. A nonlinear gain model captured population responses, revealing supralinear integration in specific laminar compartments. Chemogenetic inhibition of excitatory deep-layer neurons selectively impaired multisensory-driven orientation. Our results shed light on laminar specialization in multisensory computation.

The contribution of thalamocortical loops to sensory adaptation is poorly resolved; to clarify this, we combined optogenetic inhibition of thalamic relay neurons with mesoscale voltage imaging in awake mice during whisker stimulation. Adaptation was associated with a progressive shift from thalamus-driven to cortico-cortical propagation patterns, and targeted thalamic suppression accelerated this shift. These results indicate that adaptation involves dynamic redistribution of signal flow within thalamocortical loops.

Despite extensive mapping of the motor cortex, principles governing population activity during coordinated limb movements remain unclear; we tracked neural trajectories using large-scale electrophysiology while animals performed multi-joint tasks. Low-dimensional manifold analysis revealed conserved rotational dynamics across tasks, with task-specific expansions near movement initiation. Perturbation of trajectory curvature predicted performance variability, indicating that motor control relies on stabilizing manifold geometry.

Sleep-dependent memory consolidation involves hippocampal–cortical communication, but causal evidence for coordinated replay is still emerging; we recorded hippocampal sharp-wave ripples and prefrontal ensembles during post-learning sleep while delivering phase-aligned optogenetic stimulation. Phase-matched stimulation enhanced prefrontal replay fidelity and improved next-day recall, whereas out-of-phase stimulation disrupted replay timing. These findings provide causal support for temporally aligned hippocampal–cortical replay in consolidation.
microbiology: Biofilm resilience to antibiotics remains a central challenge in treatment; we examined how metabolic heterogeneity influences tolerance by combining fluorescent metabolic sensors with spatial transcriptomics in Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilms. Metabolically dormant subpopulations localized to oxygen-limited niches exhibited elevated expression of efflux pump genes and survived high-dose treatment. Perturbation of redox gradients reduced dormancy and restored antibiotic susceptibility, demonstrating the importance of metabolic zoning in biofilm tolerance.

Microbial electrogenesis offers potential for bioenergy, but mechanisms underlying electron transfer remain debated; we created electrode-associated Shewanella oneidensis biofilms and measured redox dynamics with scanning electrochemical microscopy. Cytochrome-rich filaments facilitated long-range electron movement, and disruption of extracellular polymeric substances impaired conductivity. Our results demonstrate how structural and molecular components integrate to support electrogenic activity.

Understanding microbial responses to heavy-metal contamination is essential for bioremediation; we profiled metal-responsive gene networks in Cu²⁺-tolerant Bacillus strains using proteomics and reporter assays. Exposure induced a coordinated activation of efflux systems, thiol-buffering enzymes, and sporulation pathways. Mutants lacking a key metallochaperone exhibited severe growth defects, confirming its central role in detoxification. These mechanisms illuminate adaptation strategies in contaminated soils.

Bacterial sporulation is a key survival strategy, but the metabolic cues triggering differentiation remain incompletely defined; we employed metabolomics and transcriptional profiling in Bacillus subtilis during nutrient depletion. A decline in branched-chain amino acid pools activated a regulatory axis involving CodY and Spo0A, driving early commitment to sporulation. Manipulating these metabolites modulated sporulation efficiency, revealing a metabolic checkpoint governing cell fate.

Horizontal gene transfer plays a major role in shaping bacterial adaptation, yet the ecological triggers controlling plasmid exchange remain poorly defined; we developed a microfluidic co-culture system to quantify plasmid transfer between soil isolates under spatially structured nutrient gradients. Using single-cell tracking and plasmid-specific reporters, we observed a sharp increase in transfer frequency at intermediate nutrient levels, coinciding with enhanced conjugation pilus expression. Our results suggest that moderate resource availability optimizes gene exchange in soil microbial communities.

The spatial organization of gut microbiota is linked to host health, yet precise microbial arrangements are poorly mapped; we used multiplexed FISH and 3D reconstruction to chart microbe–mucus interactions in mouse colon. Distinct taxa occupied sharply defined microhabitats, with mucin-degrading species forming protective barriers around the epithelium. Disruption of mucus properties redistributed taxa and increased inflammatory markers, underscoring the functional significance of spatial structuring.

Antiviral defense systems in bacteria extend beyond CRISPR–Cas, yet many remain uncharacterized; through comparative genomics and functional assays, we identified a novel abortive infection module that triggers membrane depolarization upon phage entry. Mutants lacking this module exhibited increased susceptibility across diverse phage families. This system adds to the growing repertoire of innate bacterial defenses.

Quorum sensing regulates cooperative behaviors, but environmental noise may disrupt signaling fidelity; to test this, we engineered Burkholderia thailandensis strains with tunable signal synthesis and monitored quorum responses under fluctuating nutrient regimes. Noise-strengthened environments produced hysteresis in response curves and favored phenotypes with broadened detection thresholds. We propose that ecological variability selects for robust quorum architectures.

Viruses in aquatic ecosystems drive microbial turnover, yet the infection dynamics of dominant phage groups are not well characterized; we isolated a cyanophage targeting Prochlorococcus and performed time-resolved infection assays. RNA sequencing revealed a cascade of transcriptional modules governing early host takeover, followed by synchronized virion assembly. Environmental simulations showed that diel light cycles strongly modulated burst size. These findings clarify phage–host interactions in marine phototrophs.

The emergence of multidrug-resistant Enterobacteriaceae underscores the need for novel therapeutic targets; we used transposon sequencing to identify essential genes under antibiotic stress and discovered a previously uncharacterized membrane-associated factor critical for cell envelope integrity. Structural modeling predicted a β-barrel architecture, and CRISPR-interference knockdown sensitized cells to β-lactams. Our data highlight a promising vulnerability within the cell envelope assembly pathway.
cell biology: Cell–cell junction dynamics are crucial for tissue integrity, yet the coordination of cadherin turnover during morphogenesis is not fully understood; using lattice light-sheet microscopy in developing zebrafish, we quantified E-cadherin trafficking and found pulsatile endocytosis synchronized with actomyosin contractions. Inhibiting dynamin disrupted pulsatility and impaired tissue elongation. Our findings reveal a mechano-regulated turnover mechanism enabling coordinated morphogenetic movements.

Mitochondrial quality control requires selective mitophagy, yet the determinants of organelle targeting remain unclear; using mito-pH sensors and live-cell reporters, we discovered that mild depolarization triggers transient ‘priming’ events that recruit Parkin only after repeated stress cycles. Inhibiting priming reduced mitophagy efficiency, indicating a multi-step recognition mechanism.

Secretory pathway efficiency is shaped by Golgi architecture, but how cisternal organization influences cargo flow is not fully defined; through perturbation of Golgi stacking proteins and super-resolution imaging, we found that loosening cisternal stacking accelerated cargo transit but increased sorting errors. Our findings suggest that Golgi architecture balances speed and fidelity in secretion.

Cell division fidelity depends on spindle geometry, yet the cues guiding spindle positioning during asymmetric division remain elusive; in Drosophila neuroblasts, we used photoactivatable centrosome markers to track microtubule dynamics and observed biased cortical pulling forces mediated by Pins–Gα complexes. Disrupting these interactions randomized spindle orientation and impaired fate specification, suggesting a force-based positioning mechanism.

Endosomal maturation is central to cargo sorting; we employed pH-sensitive reporters and particle tracking to quantify Rab5-to-Rab7 transition kinetics. Maturation followed a stochastic but temporally constrained sequence, with lipid-phase transitions acting as rate-limiting steps. Manipulating cholesterol levels altered these transitions, revealing lipid composition as a key determinant of endosomal identity.

Organelle contact sites orchestrate metabolic exchange, but the regulatory principles governing their formation remain unclear; we used correlative EM and optogenetic tethering to map dynamic ER–mitochondria contacts in human fibroblasts. Contacts expanded in response to Ca²⁺ bursts and lipid synthesis demand, with the tethering protein Mfn2 acting as a key modulator. Disrupting Mfn2 reduced lipid transfer efficiency, demonstrating its central role in inter-organelle communication.

Cytoskeletal remodeling underlies cell migration, but how microtubules coordinate with actin protrusions is not fully known; we combined optogenetic Rac activation with TIRF imaging to probe cross-talk in migrating epithelial cells. Microtubule growth biased protrusion stability, while localized microtubule depolymerization triggered transient actin retraction. Our results outline a feedback loop integrating microtubule dynamics with protrusive activity.

The mechanisms that maintain nuclear envelope integrity during mechanical stress are poorly resolved; we subjected mammalian cells to cyclic deformation and tracked nuclear lamina dynamics via live-cell imaging. Lamin A/C rapidly redistributed to stressed regions, while depletion of lamin A/C increased rupture frequency and impaired DNA repair. Our work highlights the lamina’s mechanical buffering as essential for genomic stability.

Autophagosome formation is tightly regulated, yet the sequence of membrane remodeling events remains debated; using high-speed cryo-CLEM, we visualized early phagophore growth and found that local PI3P enrichment precedes Atg protein assembly. Perturbation of lipid transfer proteins slowed phagophore expansion. These observations refine the timeline of autophagy initiation.

Mammalian cells respond to osmotic stress via rapid volume regulation, but the molecular mediators remain incompletely characterized; integrating ion flux measurements with single-cell proteomics, we identified a chloride channel that rapidly upregulates under hyperosmotic conditions. Channel inhibition delayed volume recovery and altered downstream MAPK signaling. These data position chloride flux as a central regulator of osmoadaptation.
bioinformatics: Single-cell chromatin accessibility data contain substantial technical noise; we created a denoising autoencoder trained to separate biological from technical variation. Application to hematopoietic progenitors recovered clearer developmental trajectories and enhanced regulatory peak detection. Our method increases signal fidelity in single-cell epigenomic analyses.

Large-scale metagenomic profiling demands efficient classification algorithms; we created a lightweight k-mer sketching method that reduces memory usage while preserving taxonomic resolution. Evaluation on diverse environmental datasets showed a >10× speed improvement with minimal loss in accuracy. This approach facilitates scalable microbiome analysis.

Accurate phylogenetic placement is essential for studying microbial evolution; we developed an alignment-free placement algorithm based on variable-length minimizers that improved placement accuracy for fragmented genomes. Benchmarking with simulated microbial communities showed robustness to contamination. Our tool supports high-throughput evolutionary analyses.

Protein structure prediction from partial constraints remains an unsolved challenge; we designed a hybrid pipeline combining contact map imputation with transformer-based folding. Testing on sparse crosslinking data improved structural accuracy relative to conventional homology models. Our method expands structure prediction to data-limited scenarios.

Reconstructing gene regulatory networks from single-cell RNA-seq remains challenging due to sparsity; we introduced a probabilistic graph model leveraging shared nearest-neighbor structure to infer regulatory edges. Applied to developing retina data, our method recovered lineage-specific regulators validated by perturbation studies. This demonstrates improved network inference in sparse datasets.

Genome assembly of complex eukaryotes is hindered by repeats; we introduced a graph simplification algorithm that resolves structural ambiguities by leveraging long-range barcode information. Assemblies of plant genomes showed improved contiguity and reduced misjoins. This approach enhances assembly robustness for repeat-rich genomes.

Functional annotation of metatranscriptomes requires distinguishing active taxa; we built a machine-learning classifier integrating taxonomic markers with expression signatures to assign transcripts to likely producers. Applied to gut microbiome time-course data, the model uncovered diel activity patterns not resolved by traditional pipelines. This framework improves interpretation of community function.

Comparative genomics relies on robust orthology detection; we developed a synteny-aware clustering algorithm that incorporates local genomic context to improve ortholog identification. Tests across vertebrate genomes revealed superior discrimination of paralogs from orthologs. The method supports more accurate evolutionary inference.

Predicting functional impacts of noncoding variants requires integrative modeling; we developed a deep attention-based network trained on chromatin accessibility, transcription factor motifs, and evolutionary conservation. Benchmarking on ENCODE datasets showed significant gains over existing models, particularly for context-specific enhancer variants. Our framework enables more accurate interpretation of noncoding genetic variation.

Integrative multi-omics analysis requires models that handle heterogeneous data; we built a variational framework linking transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic layers through latent biological processes. Applied to cancer datasets, the model identified pathway-level dysregulations predictive of treatment response. This provides a unified approach to multi-omics integration.
